page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-30-lssd is an x86_64 instance provisioned with 30 vCPUs across 15 physical cores using the AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. It features 2 threads per core, 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. System memory totals 240.0 GB, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per core). For high-throughput local disk storage, the instance includes 804 GB of NVMe SSD across 2 local drives. It does not include hardware GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng reaching 2,864.57 (top 25%). Multi-core stress-ng records 43,041.35 and Geekbench multi-core registers 14,292.0, aligning with median expectations for 30-vCPU setups. Memory subsystem evaluations highlight strong overall results in PassMark memory testing (2,792.8), alongside 2,122.74 GB/sec in cached small-block read bandwidth. However, uncached large-block write bandwidth drops to 25.09 GB/sec, placing it in the lower 25% tier.

Instruction set support covers AVX-512 extensions including AVX-512 VNNI and AVX-512 BF16, alongside AES and SHA-NI cryptographic hardware instructions. In targeted application metrics, the server delivers 38.76 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 21.89 GB/sec in static web serving. Lightweight language model evaluation highlights fast text generation on 135M models (314.87 tokens/sec), though throughput declines sharply to 7.46 tokens/sec during 70B prompt processing due to reliance strictly on CPU inference.

Given its high RAM density, dedicated AMD cores, and fast local NVMe storage, this configuration serves well for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, caching layers, and transactional database engines requiring high IOPS. The primary architectural tradeoff rests between its expansive memory footprint and lower uncached memory write bandwidth.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-30-lssd is an x86_64 server offering 30 vCPUs across 15 physical AMD EPYC 9B14 cores, 240.0 GB of memory, and 804 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Lacking discrete GPUs, it relies on AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions for acceleration. The 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio accommodates large in-memory footprints, backed by solid PassMark memory scores and top-quartile single-core stress-ng results (2,864.57). While uncached memory write throughput is comparatively limited at 25.09 GB/sec, it maintains strong throughput for Redis operations (38.76 million ops/sec) and multi-threaded decompression. The instance fits memory-heavy enterprise databases, intermediate analytics pipelines, caching clusters, and I/O-intensive workloads needing high-speed local disk storage.
